applicable_programme.grade_mapping_note: The public MYP page describes the programme as for students aged 11-16 and as a five-year programme that schools may shorten. Mapping Grade 7 (often about ages 12-13) onto that span is our convention, not an IB grade or MYP-year boundary.

grade_specific_note.label: C
grade_specific_note.text: Florida Grade 7 mathematics is grade-coded (MA.7), not a named high-school course. MYP mathematics can be standard or extended. That choice is a school decision and is not made here.

subject_group_or_structure.mapping_to_primer_subject: Grade 7 Florida mathematics (MA.7) is mapped here to the MYP mathematics subject group. The public page names the branches number, algebra, geometry and trigonometry, and statistics and probability, and two levels of challenge (standard and extended). It does not place Grade 7 in either level.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The International Baccalaureate® (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) is for students aged 11-16.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The MYP is a five-year programme, which can be implemented in a partnership between schools, or in several abbreviated (two, three or four year) formats.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Developing and applying these social, thinking, research, communication and self management skills helps students learn how to learn.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Using global contexts, MYP students develop an understanding of their common humanity and shared guardianship of the planet through developmentally appropriate explorations of: identities and relationships; personal and cultural expression; orientations in space and time; scientific and technical innovation; fairness and development; globalization and sustainability.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The MYP prescribes sixteen key interdisciplinary concepts along with related concepts for each discipline.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: MYP teachers assess the prescribed subject-group objectives using the assessment criteria for each subject group in each year of the programme.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: In the International Baccalaureate® (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP), mathematics promotes both inquiry and application, helping students to develop problem solving techniques that transcend the discipline and that are useful in the world beyond school.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The MYP mathematics framework encompasses number, algebra, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: In the MYP, the topics and skills in the framework for mathematics are organized so that students can work at two levels of challenge: standard mathematics and extended mathematics.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The mathematics subject brief names four equally weighted assessment criteria: A Knowing and understanding; B Investigating patterns; C Communicating; D Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The 1-8 band descriptors are not stored here.

typical_fit.label: C
typical_fit.text: Grade 7 Florida mathematics in this draft covers equivalent forms of rational numbers, operations with rational numbers, linear expressions, one-step inequalities and two-step equations, percentages and proportions, proportional relationships, area including circles, surface area and volume of right circular cylinders, and probability. Those ceilings are Florida’s. A reasonable MYP fit is the number, algebra, geometry, and statistics branches, plus criteria A and D, without claiming IB sets the same grade-7 limits or chooses standard versus extended mathematics for this grade.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.label: C

florida.alignment_note: Laws of Exponents with whole-number exponents and rational bases fit the number branch and criterion A. The exponent and base limits are Florida’s.
Adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing rational numbers with procedural fluency is Florida language. MYP does not publish that fluency label.
Writing and solving one-step inequalities can sit under criterion A. The one-step limit and the listed inequality forms are Florida’s.
Deciding whether two quantities are proportional fits relationships as an example key concept. The table, graph, or description rule is Florida’s.
Circumference and diameter of circles fit geometry. The MYP branch name also includes trigonometry, which this Florida grade list does not require.
Volume of right circular cylinders is a Florida benchmark. The public MYP pages do not name that solid.
Theoretical probability of a simple experiment fits statistics and probability. That experiment list is Florida’s, not a quoted MYP outcome.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.notes: Arizona standards deferred. These rows are suggested starting points (Label C), not an official IB-Florida crosswalk.
